facts.raw_span: recurrent abdominal pain and syncope after drinking alcohol
symptoms persisting for 2 years but worsening on admission
symptoms usually occurred 6-20 hours after alcohol ingestion and lasted 5-10 minutes
syncope occurred only after large alcohol intake
hypertension diagnosed 3 months prior
smoking and alcohol overconsumption (250g/week) for about 20 years
No specific physical examination findings were documented in the case report
High-sensitivity troponin I: 0.01 ng/mL (normal)
Serum potassium: 4.6 mEq/L (normal)
High-degree atrioventricular block and premature ventricular contractions
ST segments elevated 4-6 mm in leads II, III and aVF, with ST depression in leads V2-V6
10% stenosis in proximal left anterior descending artery (LAD) and right coronary artery (RCA)

rationales.F01: Alcoholic cardiomyopathy is suggested by symptoms occurring after alcohol ingestion
rationales.F03: Timing of symptoms after alcohol ingestion may indicate an alcohol-related condition
rationales.F04: Syncope after large alcohol intake may indicate an alcohol-related cardiac condition
rationales.F06: Long-term heavy alcohol use is a risk factor for alcoholic cardiomyopathy and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease
rationales.F10: High-degree atrioventricular block and premature ventricular contractions are indicative of cardiac dysfunction
rationales.F11: ST segment elevations are indicative of cardiac ischemia, which may be related to variant angina or other cardiac conditions
rationales.F12: Mild stenosis in coronary arteries is not typical of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, reducing its likelihood
